Definition: properly, to fasten up, i.e. with a bar or cord; hence, to sandal, i.e. furnish with slippers
BiblicalUsage: Na'al as a verb means to fasten up or furnish with sandals, and it also means to bolt a door shut. In 2 Chronicles 28:15 the men of Judah take the captives, clothe them, and shod them before sending them home, and in 2 Samuel 13:17 Amnon orders the door bolted after Tamar.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the same word can dress a wound or slam a door, and the difference is the heart behind it; kindness puts shoes on bare feet; cruelty bolts the door on the one it has hurt.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
